WITH scored AS (
 SELECT t.observstation, s.signalregistry,
 (p.techsigprob * 4 + p.biosigprob / 100 + p.sigunique * 2 + p.anomscore / 2) * (1 - p.falseposprob) AS rpi,
 (1 - p.falseposprob) * d.decodeconf * CASE WHEN s.snrratio - 0.1 * ABS(s.noisefloordbm) > 0 THEN (s.snrratio - 0.1 * ABS(s.noisefloordbm)) / 10 + 0.5 ELSE 0.1 END AS ccs_approx
 FROM signals s
 JOIN telescopes t ON t.telescregistry = s.telescref
 LEFT JOIN signalprobabilities p ON p.signalref = s.signalregistry
 LEFT JOIN signaldecoding d ON d.signalref = s.signalregistry
)
SELECT o.observstation AS observatory_name,
 COUNT(s.signalregistry) AS total_signal_count,
 AVG(s.rpi) AS average_priority_score,
 AVG(s.ccs_approx) AS average_ccs_approx,
 COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.rpi > 3) AS important_signal_count,
 COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.ccs_approx > 0.8) AS high_confidence_signal_count,
 COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.rpi > 3 AND s.ccs_approx > 0.8) AS promising_signal_count
FROM observatories o
LEFT JOIN scored s ON s.observstation = o.observstation
GROUP BY o.observstation
ORDER BY promising_signal_count DESC;

    SELECT t.observstation, s.signalregistry,
           (p.techsigprob * 4 + p.biosigprob / 100 + p.sigunique * 2 + p.anomscore / 2) * (1 - p.falseposprob) AS rpi,
           (1 - p.falseposprob) * d.decodeconf * CASE WHEN s.snrratio - 0.1 * ABS(s.noisefloordbm) > 0 THEN (s.snrratio - 0.1 * ABS(s.noisefloordbm)) / 10 + 0.5 ELSE 0.1 END AS ccs_approx
    FROM signals s
    JOIN telescopes t ON t.telescregistry = s.telescref
    JOIN signalprobabilities p ON p.signalref = s.signalregistry
    JOIN signaldecoding d ON d.signalref = s.signalregistry
)
SELECT o.observstation AS observatory_name,
       COUNT(*) AS total_signal_count,
       AVG(s.rpi) AS average_priority_score,
       AVG(s.ccs_approx) AS average_ccs_approx,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.rpi > 3) AS important_signal_count,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.ccs_approx > 0.8) AS high_confidence_signal_count,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE s.rpi > 3 AND s.ccs_approx > 0.8) AS promising_signal_count
FROM observatories o
JOIN scored s ON s.observstation = o.observstation
GROUP BY o.observstation
ORDER BY promising_signal_count DESC;

args.question: How should the priority score be calculated, and what priority criteria make a signal 'important'?

tool_trajectory.result:
The priority score is computed as a Research Priority Index (RPI) that combines several signal probability factors: it weights TechSigProb (×4), BioSigProb (÷100), SigUnique (×2), and AnomScore (÷2), then multiplies the sum by (1 − FalsePosProb) to penalize likely false positives.

A signal is considered "important" (high-priority) when its RPI exceeds 3. Signals are also flagged as high-confidence when their approximate Confirmation Confidence Score (CCS) exceeds 0.8, and the most valuable ones are those meeting both criteria (RPI > 3 AND CCS > 0.8).

 SELECT t.observstation, s.signalregistry,
 (p.techsigprob * 4 + p.biosigprob / 100 + p.sigunique * 2 + p.anomscore / 2) * (1 - p.falseposprob) AS rpi,

FROM observatories o

args.question: How should the priority score be calculated, and what priority criteria make a signal 'important'?

tool_trajectory.result:
The priority score is computed as a Research Priority Index (RPI) that combines several signal probability factors: it weights TechSigProb (×4), BioSigProb (÷100), SigUnique (×2), and AnomScore (÷2), then multiplies the sum by (1 − FalsePosProb) to penalize likely false positives.

A signal is considered "important" (high-priority) when its RPI exceeds 3. Signals are also flagged as high-confidence when their approximate Confirmation Confidence Score (CCS) exceeds 0.8, and the most valuable ones are those meeting both criteria (RPI > 3 AND CCS > 0.8).
